features: Free Download - Game Review An asteroid of 5,000,000 m³ will hit Earth in 90 days. The government already spent 90 days arguing about who pays. Then one miner came to the tender with his own pickaxe. He asked for no money and said the asteroid would pay for itself. The vote was unanimous, for the first time in history. You are that miner. Every day you fly down and dig while your air lasts. Back on the ship you sell the ore and buy bigger tools and guns. A big counter shows how many m³ are left. On the first day it hardly moves. Later your ship fires at the rock while you dig, and the number goes down much faster. You start with the pickaxe you brought. The last tool is a swarm of small homing missiles. Big pieces break off and float away, and you can ride them. Earth has rockets that are already paid for, but they are aimed at the neighbors. So your ship starts with no guns, and you buy them with the ore money. They fire at the asteroid on their own. The most expensive one shoots a black hole into the rock.The contract is for one miner, but the government does not check how many came. Up to 8 players can dig the same asteroid in online co-op. The pay is still zero. The ore money goes into one wallet, and the host decides who can spend it. Anyone who sits in the lander can start a 10-second count, or kick a friend out of the hatch. If you are not in the lander when it leaves the asteroid, you black out and lose your cargo. The campaign is the host's save, and guests keep their own game. What you find in the rock goes to the ship's museum, like an empty safe labeled "Asteroid defense budget". From the observation dome you can see Earth through a telescope. A crowd holds KEEP WORKING signs. Bookmakers take bets on you. The government meets on a beach. The plot at the impact point is already sold, and the owners rave about the sky view. After the main contract, other clients send offers. A space hotel wants a duck-shaped asteroid gone, because guests say it keeps staring at them. Singleplayer, or online co-op forup to 8 players. Alone, the main contract takes about 6 to 9 hours.

features: Free Download - Game Review In the last nine years of LEGO games, we've come to associate the iconic plastic building bricks with not just creativity, but also silly, lighthearted humor. The LEGO Movie Videogame attempts to bring the wonderful film's consistently joyful and entertaining story and heroes into the same gaming format we’ve seen from developer TT Games’ series. But while it delivers some amusing scenarios across diverse terrain, the premise feels overextended. However, it ends up showing that one of the strengths of other LEGO games is the charm that comes from recreating a non-LEGO scene in amusing ways. This one is just retreading the same material, and there’s not much of it to draw from. Where the strong recent LEGO Marvel and DC games had decades of comics and scads of heroes and villains to work with, The LEGO Movie Videogame has but a single movie script – albeit a pretty excellent one. While the game maintains a generally amusing tone and includes some enjoyable peaks – such as commanding Uni-Kitty's startling alternate form, or bashing through levels as a massive, Transformers-esque robot pirate – trying to turn a succinct, 90-minute film into a seven-hour game campaign means it inevitably drags in spots.
